query_text: Need a web app for my illustration commissions that actually has some soul to it — a place where people can see my different tier offerings laid out clearly and join a waitlist if all slots are full, the kind of site that feels like it belongs to a real artist and not just a generic booking form.

Create a web app for an independent SEO consultant that has the kind of quiet confidence a real expert carries — a place where visitors can claim a free audit offer and leave their contact details, with the identity of the tool feeling polished and intentional rather than like a thrown-together lead magnet.

A portfolio app for a freelance data scientist that lives in the browser and actually has a point of view — where each project has a live interactive demo embedded right in the page so visitors can poke around the work themselves, and the whole thing feels curated rather than just a résumé dump.

A voiceover artist showcase app for desktop browsers that has a real identity to it — where visitors can listen to demo reels organized by style or genre, and there's a clear rate card on the same page so people know what they're getting into, the kind of tool that feels like it was built by someone with taste.

Create a web app for a freelance content creator that feels like a real media kit and not just another contact form — somewhere brands can browse past partnership work, get a sense of the creator's identity and reach, and then send a collaboration or press inquiry, all from a single desktop-first site that has its own distinct personality.

Need a web app that lets an independent architect stop juggling back-and-forth emails just to set up a first meeting — clients should be able to pick a time slot from a live availability calendar on the site, answer a few basic questions about their project, and confirm the consultation booking all by themselves from a desktop browser.

Need a web app that takes the headache out of scheduling private yoga sessions — students pick a time from the instructor's available slots, choose a session length, and confirm the booking without any messages going back and forth, all from a browser so the instructor stops spending half their day on appointment logistics.

Build a web app that makes booking a notary appointment as painless as possible — clients pick a date, drop in their document type, and confirm a time without any phone tag involved, and the notary can see all upcoming appointments in one tidy list on the same browser-based tool.

A scheduling app for an immigration consultant that lives in the browser — clients land on the site, pick an open time slot for a case review, fill in a short form with their visa category and situation, and book a session without anyone needing to play phone tag or send follow-up emails to confirm.

Build a web app that lets a freelance data analyst stop wasting time on back-and-forth just to set up a call — clients visit the site in their desktop browser, pick a time slot from a real calendar of available hours, describe what kind of data problem they have, and lock in a consultation booking on the spot.

Need a web app that handles all the back-and-forth of booking a private chef dinner experience without any of the hassle — guests visit the site, browse available dates, pick a menu style or occasion type, and reserve their slot right there in the browser, so the chef doesn't have to chase down confirmations through text.

Build a web app for an independent interior designer that ends the back-and-forth of setting up a first room consultation — homeowners visit the site, pick an open slot from a live schedule, note the room they need help with, and confirm the booking right in the browser without any follow-up needed.

Need a web app for a deep work and productivity course aimed at working professionals — it should have a clear list of lessons and modules, let learners track which sections they've finished, and include a spot for key takeaways or notes on each topic, all accessible from a desktop browser in one tidy place.

A coaching platform app for public speaking and presentation skills built for independent professionals, where you can browse a list of available courses and coaches, see what each one covers, sign up for a session, and track your progress through the material — runs in a desktop browser and keeps everything in one organized spot.

Create a web app that works as a personal brand and thought leadership course hub — a clear list of courses you can browse, a way to track what you've completed, and a spot for the key lessons so nothing gets lost, all organized in a desktop-friendly layout that's easy to navigate.

Need a web app that helps practitioners actually get through research papers — you paste in a paper or drop in a link, it breaks the content into digestible chunks with the key findings highlighted, and you can save your own notes or starred passages in a reading list you can come back to, all from a desktop browser.

Build a web app for freelancers who want to figure out how to price their work and compare their rates against what others in their field charge — a clear list of pricing strategies to learn from, a simple tool to punch in your own numbers, and a way to see how you stack up, all accessible in a desktop browser.

Create a web app where people from different fields can list what skills they're willing to teach and what they want to learn, browse other members' offers, and arrange a skill swap — organized in a clear list view in the desktop browser so you can quickly see who has what and who wants what.

A reference app for freelance designers where you can browse a library of common interface patterns organized by category, and each one has a short video walkthrough showing how it works in practice — runs in a desktop browser and is easy to scroll through when you need a quick reference without leaving your work.

Make a web app for freelance educators and online course creators to hang out and work together — a place in the browser where people can post ideas for collaborations, share resources they've built, and find others who want to co-teach or bundle their stuff, kind of like a small forum but just for the teaching creator crowd.

Build a web app where independent researchers can share their data sets and findings with each other and get informal peer feedback — a community site for desktop browsers where you can post your work, leave comments on others' studies, and find people working on similar topics to compare notes with.

Make a web app where solopreneurs can share and find contract templates and useful legal clause examples — a community hub in the browser where people can upload the bits they've found helpful, browse what others have contributed, and leave comments so everyone's getting a bit of collective wisdom without paying a lawyer every time.

A community app for freelance video editors in the browser where you can post your showreel or a clip you've been working on, get honest written feedback from other editors, and browse what everyone else is putting up — kind of like a critique circle but online and specifically for people who do this kind of work for a living.

Create a web app for independent brand strategists where they can share case studies of their work, browse what others have done for inspiration, and leave comments or questions on each other's projects — a community site for desktop browsers that works kind of like a portfolio network but specifically for strategy work.

Make a web app where remote freelancers can find local coworking spots near them and connect with other freelancers who are already working there — a browser-based community tool where you can browse spaces by area, see who else is a regular there, and maybe coordinate showing up at the same time so you're not always working alone.
